Axtron browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Axtron DST-5 Distortion Published on December 5, 2010 Axtron distortion pedal Information The Axtron DST-5 Distortion is an analog effects pedal from a family of Japanese-made compact distortion units produced during the 1980s and distributed under multiple brand names including Cutec, Profile+, Columbus, Pick Boy, and Vision. Designed for electric guitar and keyboard, the DST-5 offers a versatile range of drive tones from mild overdrive to saturated distortion, with a simple control layout that makes it easy to dial in a variety of textures suited to rock, pop, and early metal tones. The circuit delivers a harmonically rich distortion with a slightly fuzzy edge, combining moderate compression with a responsive gain structure that reacts dynamically to player input. The three-knob interface includes Level, Tone, and Distortion controls, allowing precise adjustment of output volume, EQ brightness, and gain intensity. The resulting sound is reminiscent of contemporary Japanese analog circuits inspired by pedals such as the DOD 250 and early Boss DS-1, offering a gritty but musical distortion character with strong midrange presence. The DST-5 is housed in a molded plastic chassis with a metal baseplate, incorporating a large treadle-style footswitch for activation. A red LED indicator displays effect status, and a rear sliding battery compartment allows easy access for 9V power. Some versions support external DC operation. The compact and lightweight design made it an affordable yet functional pedal for both beginners and working musicians during the era.
